elements.content: Communication Goal: I can tell a simple story about the past and ask about past events.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 8. People around you
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: How I met my friend
- Materials: Timeline, photo prompts, story cards, COSYmanuals 'past simple' and 'there was/were' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use was/were to talk about past states
• narrate a simple past story
• ask Did you...? and Wh- questions about the past

Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (18 items):

met — the past of 'meet'. Example: I met my friend at school.
school — a place where children learn. Example: We were at school together.
class — a group of students, or a lesson. Example: We are in the same class.
years ago — a time in the past. Example: I met her five years ago.
become — to start to be something. Example: We became close friends.
best friend — the friend you like most. Example: She is my best friend.
friend — a person you like and know well. Example: Tom is my best friend.
close — near or emotionally connected. Example: We are a close family.
together — with each other. Example: We eat together every evening.
nice — pleasant or kind. Example: She is a nice person.
was — the past of am and is. Example: I was at home yesterday.
were — the past of are. Example: They were at school.
didn't — the short negative past helper. Example: I didn't see her yesterday.
did — the past helper for questions. Example: Did you meet your friend?
yesterday — the day before today. Example: I was at home yesterday.
last week — the week before this week. Example: Last week, I visited my family.
ago — before now. Example: I met her five years ago.
introduce — to tell people someone's name. Example: Let me introduce my friend.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I met my best friend at school five years ago. (starting a story)
• We were in the same class. (giving background)
• We became close friends. (describing a change)
• Where were you yesterday? (asking about a past place)
• Did you meet your friend last week? (asking a past yes/no question)
• What did you do? (asking about a past action)
• I didn't see her yesterday. (past negative)

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use the past simple to talk about finished actions in the past.

Form:
Past simple: regular verbs: Regular verbs add -ed: work → worked. Negative: didn't + base verb. Question: Did + subject + base verb?

Examples:
• I worked yesterday.
• She visited her friend.
• We didn't watch TV.
• Did you call him?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I ___ my friend yesterday.
She ___ TV last night.
We ___ work on Sunday.
___ you call him?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• Yesterday, I ... (work / visit / play) ...
• Last weekend, she ...
• I didn't ... yesterday.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What did you do yesterday?
• Where did you go last weekend?
• Did you study English last week?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about yesterday with regular past verbs.
• Write three sentences about last weekend.
Reading: How I met my friend

I met my best friend at school five years ago. We were in the same class. She was shy, and I was new. We sat together and talked. We became close friends. We played football and studied together. Yesterday, I saw her at the park. We were happy. Did you meet your best friend at school? Where were you yesterday? What did you do last weekend?
Where did they meet?
Where was the writer yesterday?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: How did you meet your best friend?
B: I met her at school five years ago. We were in the same class.
A: Were you friends then?
B: Yes, we were. We became close friends.
A: What did you do together?
B: We played football and studied together. Yesterday, we were at the park.
Where did the speaker meet her friend?
Were they in the same class?
Speaking task: Tell your partner how you met a friend. Ask three past questions about their story.

• How did you meet your best friend?
• Where were you?
• What did you do together?
• Did you meet your friend last week?
• Why is this friendship important?
Role-play: You are at a reunion. Tell a group the story of how you met your best friend and answer their past questions.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about how you met a friend. Use was/were, a past verb, and one past question.
Model: I met ... We were ... I didn't ... Did you ...?
